q: Work must be done to separate two bodies having opposite charges since they ____ each other.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Work must be done to separate two bodies having opposite charges since they attract each other.

q: Likewise, work must be done to bring closer two bodies having the same kind of charge since they ____ each other.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Likewise, work must be done to bring closer two bodies having the same kind of charge since they repel each other.

q: In both cases the work done is stored up in the charged objects as ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In both cases the work done is stored up in the charged objects as electric potential energy.

q: The work done in bringing the charge q against the electric force from ____ to a point in an electric field is the electric potential energy of charge q at that point.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The work done in bringing the charge q against the electric force from infinity to a point in an electric field is the electric potential energy of charge q at that point.

q: The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the work done in bringing a ____ against the electric force from infinity to that point.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge against the electric force from infinity to that point.

q: Then the electric potential at that point can be expressed as, $V = $ ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Then the electric potential at that point can be expressed as, V = (W)/(q).

q: Since the electric potential is actually the amount of work done, it is a ____ quantity.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Since the electric potential is actually the amount of work done, it is a scalar quantity.

q: The electric potential is the ____ per unit positive charge.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential is the electric potential energy per unit positive charge.

q: The electric potential at infinity is taken as ____ by convention.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential at infinity is taken as zero by convention.

q: The practical unit of electric potential is the ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The practical unit of electric potential is the volt (V).

q: If the work done in bringing +1 coulomb from infinity to a point in an electric field is 1 joule, the electric potential at that point is 1 joule per coulomb ($1 J C^{-1}$) or ____.
e: Coulomb's law: F = K q1 q2 / r². Like charges repel; unlike charges attract. If the work done in bringing +1 coulomb from infinity to a point in an electric field is 1 joule, the electric potential at that point is 1 joule per coulomb (1 J C^-1) or 1 V.

q: The electric potential difference between two points in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one point to another against ____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric potential difference between two points in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one point to another against electric force.

q: The SI unit of electric potential difference is ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The SI unit of electric potential difference is volt.

q: A positive charge will move from a point of ____ to a point of lower electric potential.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. A positive charge will move from a point of higher electric potential to a point of lower electric potential.

q: A negative charge will move from a point of lower electric potential to a point of ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. A negative charge will move from a point of lower electric potential to a point of higher electric potential.

q: The electric potential at a distance r from a point charge +Q can be expressed as $V = $ ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential at a distance r from a point charge +Q can be expressed as V = (1)/(4 π ε_0) (Q)/(r).

q: Therefore, the electric potential V at a point is ____ to the charge Q and inversely proportional to the distance r from the charge.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Therefore, the electric potential V at a point is directly proportional to the charge Q and inversely proportional to the distance r from the charge. Directly proportional is the term used with Therefore, electric potential V at point.

q: Therefore, the electric potential V at a point is directly proportional to the charge Q and ____ to the distance r from the charge.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Therefore, the electric potential V at a point is directly proportional to the charge Q and inversely proportional to the distance r from the charge. Inversely proportional is the term used with Therefore, electric potential V at point.

q: In doing so the ____ of the individual charges must be taken into account.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In doing so the signs of the individual charges must be taken into account.

q: That is to say the individual electric potentials must be added ____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. That is to say the individual electric potentials must be added algebraically.

q: The work done is ____ by the charge, it only depends on the electric potential difference between two points.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The work done is independent of the path taken by the charge, it only depends on the electric potential difference between two points.
